rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses cast a divinely shown branch into the water, which became sweet; God taught him statutes and ordinances there.
rows.anchor: فأظهر الرب له عودا فألقاه في الماء , فعذب الماء هناك , علمه السنن والأحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel camped at Elim, where twelve water springs and seventy palm trees stood.
rows.anchor: وكان هناك اثنتا عشرة عينا من ماء وسبعون نخلة فنزلوا هناك على الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They reached the wilderness of Sin between Elim and Sinai on the fifteenth day of the second month after leaving Egypt.
rows.anchor: فأتوا برية سينين التي بين آليم وسينين في خمسة عشر من الشهر الثاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron, longing for Egypt's meat and bread and accusing them of bringing the people into the wilderness to die of hunger.
rows.anchor: كنا نحب أن نتوفى في أرض مصر إذ كنا جلوسا بين أيدينا مراجل اللحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promised bread from heaven and daily gathering as a test of whether Israel would keep his commands.
rows.anchor: ها أنا ذا مهبط لكم الخبز من السماء فليخرج الشعب فليلتقطوا طعام يوم بيوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commanded a double collection on the sixth day.
rows.anchor: فإذا كان اليوم السادس فليعدوا فضلا على ما يأتون به وليكن ذلك ضعف ما يلتقطون في كل يوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses and Aaron told the people that God had brought them from Egypt and that they would see his glory the next morning; their complaint had reached him.
rows.anchor: تعلمون أن الرب أخرجكم من أرض مصر وبالغداة تعاينون مجد الرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses said God would give meat in the evening and bread in the morning, and that the people's complaint was against God rather than his messengers.
rows.anchor: وليس إنما تتذمرون علينا بل على الرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron brought the congregation near; God's glory appeared in a cloud, and God said he had heard their grumbling.
rows.anchor: فلما قال هارون ذلك لجميع جماعة بني إسرائيل التفتوا فإذا مجد الرب قد اعتلن في السحاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promised evening meat and morning bread so Israel would know that he was their Lord.
rows.anchor: عند مغارب الشمس تأكلون اللحم وبالغداة شرقا تشبعون من الخبز فتعلمون أني أنا الرب إلهكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quail covered the camp at evening, and morning dew surrounded it before manna appeared.
rows.anchor: فلما كان عند الأصيل صعدت السماني فتغشت العسكر , وكان بالغداة ضبابة تقطر المن فأحاطت بالعسكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The manna appeared as flaky material on the ground, resembling frost.
rows.anchor: فإذا على وجه الأرض دقيق يتقشر وكان شبه صفائح الجليد على الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses identified the manna as God's bread and instructed each person to gather one measure according to need for every member of the household.
rows.anchor: ليلتقط المرء منه على قدر قوته مكيالا لكل نفس على عدد رؤوسكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although some gathered much and others little, the measured amounts left no surplus for the first or shortage for the latter.
rows.anchor: فلم يفضل الذي أخذ الكثير والذي أخذ القليل لم يعدمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some disobeyed Moses by keeping manna overnight; it became wormy and foul, angering Moses.
rows.anchor: فلم يطيعوا موسى فأفضل رهط منهم للغد , فدب فيه الدود وأنتن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Manna was gathered each morning and melted when the sun grew hot.
rows.anchor: وكان إذا حميت عليه الشمس يميع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the sixth day each person gathered two measures; Moses explained that the next day was a holy Sabbath of rest.
rows.anchor: فلما كان اليوم السادس التقطوا من الخبز ضعفي ما كانوا يتناولون كل رجل مكيالين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people were to bake and cook what they needed and keep the remainder cold for the following day.
rows.anchor: وكل ما أردتم أن تختبزوه فاخبزوه واطبخوا ما أردتم طبخه واحتفظوا بما تفضلون باردا للغد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The saved manna did not spoil; Moses said to eat it on the Sabbath, when none could be gathered in the field, and to gather on the other six days.
rows.anchor: فلم ينتن ولم يدب فيه الدود فقال لهم موسى : كلوه يومكم هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some went out to gather on the seventh day but found none; God rebuked their refusal to accept his commands, and the people rested.
rows.anchor: حتى متى يأبوا أن يقبلوا وصاياي وسنني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel called the food manna; it resembled a coriander seed and tasted like honey.
rows.anchor: فسماه بنو إسرائيل المن وهو كحبة الكزبرة وطعمه كشهد العسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fourth book describes manna as coriander-like and white like the mahā, then ground, pounded, cooked into a dish, and tasting like oil-kneaded bread.
rows.anchor: والمن كان يشبه حبة الكزبرة وكان منظره أبيض كالمها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel ate manna for forty years, until reaching inhabited territory and Canaan.
rows.anchor: فأكل بنو إسرائيل المن أربعين سنة ولم يزالوا يأكلون المن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The measure is glossed as ten jarīb, that is, ten waybas.
rows.anchor: وكان ذلك المكيال عشر جريب أي عشر ويبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel moved from the wilderness of Sin to Rephidim, where there was no water to drink.
rows.anchor: فوردوا رفيدين ولم يكن للشعب ماء يشربون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people demanded water; Moses rebuked their grumbling and asked why they tested God.
rows.anchor: فقال : ما بالكم تضجون وكم تجربون الرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As thirst worsened, the people accused Moses of bringing their children and livestock out of Egypt to die; Moses feared they would stone him and prayed.
rows.anchor: لم أصعدتنا من أرض مصر لتقتلنا وأبناءنا ومواشينا بالعطش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God told Moses to take the staff used to split the sea and go ahead with Israel's elders to Horeb, where God would stand on the rock.
rows.anchor: جز قدام الشعب وانطلق ببعض أشياخ بني إسرائيل والعصا التي ضربت بها البحر ففلقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses was to strike the rock at Horeb so that water would come out for the people.
rows.anchor: فاضرب عند ذلك الظران فيخرج الماء ويشرب الشعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The place was called Massah and Meribah because Israel disputed and tested God.
rows.anchor: فسمى ذلك الموضع التجري والتذمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At Rephidim the people asked whether God was among them.
rows.anchor: وقالوا : هل الله بيننا أم لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the third month after leaving Egypt, Israel moved from Rephidim into the Sinai wilderness and camped opposite the mountain.
rows.anchor: ولما كان في الشهر الثالث بعد خروج بني إسرائيل من مصر انتهوا إلى برية سيناء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God recalled carrying Israel as on eagles' wings and bringing them to himself, then promised special favor among peoples if they obeyed and kept the covenant.
rows.anchor: فإن أنتم الآن أطعتم قولي وحفظتم عهدي فأنتم أحب إلي من جميع شعوب الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses relayed God's words to the elders, and all the people promised to do what God commanded.
rows.anchor: فأجاب الشعب كلهم جميعا وقالوا : نحن فاعلون جميع ما أمرنا به الرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God spoke to Moses in a dark cloud so the people would hear and trust him permanently.
rows.anchor: ها أنا ذا مناجيك في سحابة مظلمة لكي يسمع الشعب كلامي إذا كلمتك فيقبلوا كلامك ويصدقوك إلى الأبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people were to consecrate themselves, wash and whiten their clothes, and prepare for the third day.
rows.anchor: طهرهم اليوم وغدا وليبيضوا ثيابهم ويرحضوها وليستعدوا في اليوم الثالث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were warned not to climb the mountain or approach its boundary; anyone who came near was to be killed.
rows.anchor: احذروا أن تصعدوا إلى الجبل ولا تقربوا إلى حافاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses told the people to prepare for the third day and abstain from approaching women.
rows.anchor: كونوا مستعدين في اليوم الثالث , لا تقتربن إلى امرأة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the third day, horns, lightning, a great cloud, and a loud trumpet terrified the camp as Moses brought the people to meet God.
rows.anchor: فإذا هم بأصوات قرون وبروق وإذا هم أيضا بسحابة عظيمة قد حلت على الجبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God descended on Sinai in fire, making it smoke and tremble as the trumpet sounded.
rows.anchor: وكان جبل سيناء يخرج منه القتار والدخان , لأن الرب هبط عليه بالنار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God sent Moses down to warn the people not to break through to see him, lest many die.
rows.anchor: وأنذرهم أن لا يتزحزحوا عند النظر بين يدي الرب فيهلك منهم كثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people stood far away and asked Moses to speak for them so God would not speak directly and they would die.
rows.anchor: كلمنا أنت حتى نسمع ولا يكلمنا الله لكيلا نموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses said God spoke to test them and teach reverence so they would not sin; the people stayed back while Moses entered the cloud.
rows.anchor: إن الله إنما كلمكم ليمتحنكم ويجربكم لكي تخافوه وترهبوه ولا تخطئوا ولا تأثموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God reminded Israel that he had spoken from heaven and prohibited making gods of gold or silver.
rows.anchor: قد رايتم وعلمتم أني كلمتكم من السماء , لا تتخذوا معي آلهة من ذهب ولا تعملوا لكم آلهة من فضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promised to send a king or angel ahead to guard Israel and bring them to the prepared land, warning them to heed him because God's name rested on him.
rows.anchor: ها أنا ذا مرسل إليك الملك بين يديك ليحفظك في سفرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One version reads that the destination was the land God had prepared, with the wording ثيأته.
rows.anchor: البلد الذي أتقنت - وفي نسخة : الذي ثيأته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If Israel obeyed the messenger, God would oppose its enemies and lead the kingdom ahead; he would send fear and gradually remove the peoples, rather than destroy them in one year and leave the land desolate before Israel grew strong.
rows.anchor: ولا أبيدهم في سنة واحدة لكي لا تخرب الأرض بل رويدا رويدا حتى تعتز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another version reads تكثر in place of تعتز; Israel's boundaries run from the Sea of Reeds to Palestine and from the wilderness to the river, glossed elsewhere as the Euphrates.
rows.anchor: وفي نسخة : تكثر - فتصير ذا بطش فترث الأرض واجعل تخومك من بحر سوف إلى فلسطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy elders were to ascend and bow from afar, while Moses alone approached God.
rows.anchor: اصعد غلى الجبل انت وهارون وناذاب وآبيهوا وسبعون رجلا من أشياخ بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses recited the covenant and laws, built an altar and twelve pillars for Israel's tribes, and the people affirmed the covenant after he read it aloud.
rows.anchor: فنادى الشعب كلهم بصوت عال وقالوا : نحن نفعل ما أمرنا الرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses sprinkled the people with sacrificial blood as the blood of the covenant.
rows.anchor: فتناول موسى ذلك الدم - يعني دم القربان - فرشه على الشعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cloud covered Sinai for six days; God's glory appeared like consuming fire, and Moses remained on the mountain forty days and nights.
rows.anchor: فدخل موسى في جوف السحاب وصعد إلى الجبل فمكث موسى في الجبل أربعين يوما نهارا وأربعين ليلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God requested contributions from adult men and ordered a sanctuary made according to the pattern shown on the mountain, so he could dwell among Israel.
rows.anchor: فليخصوا لي تزكية أموالهم , وخذ ذلك من كل رجل بلغ أشده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Five additional peoples followed the Amorites in the promised conquest.
rows.anchor: وذكر بعدهم خمس فرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God instructed that the ark be made from shittim wood to the shown pattern, with specified dimensions, gold plating, rings, and carrying poles.
rows.anchor: اعمل على المثال الذي أريكه في الجبل وليتخذوا تابوتا من خشب الشمشاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ark held the testimony and was called the Ark of Testimony.
rows.anchor: وتضع الشهادة التي أعطيتك في التابوت , وسمي هذا تابوت الشهادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two gold cherubim stood on either side of the cover with wings spread above it and faces turned toward each other.
rows.anchor: واتخذ كروبين أي شخصين من ذهب اتخذهما مفرعين مصبوبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord ordered a court for the tent toward the south and described its columns, curtains, implements, service, offerings, and placement in the camp over about fifteen folios.
rows.anchor: استمر يصف له عمل هذه القبة وأعمدتها وستورها وآلاتها وخدمها وما يقرب فيها ومحل ضربها من العسكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the tent was called قبة الزمان and notes that over ten further folios describe furnishings and related structures.
rows.anchor: في نحو خمس عشرة ورقة وسماها قبة الزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God would meet and speak above the cover between the cherubim, receive a perpetual offering, sanctify the tent, and dwell among Israel as the Lord who brought them from Egypt.
rows.anchor: فأتقدس بكرامتي وأحل بين بني إسرائيل فيعلمون أني أنا الرب إلههم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text specifies a ransom contribution from the rich and poor when Israel is counted, to guard against plague.
rows.anchor: وأن الزكاة على الغني والمسكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bezalel of Judah was selected and endowed with God's spirit, wisdom, and knowledge for skilled work in metal, stone, and wood.
rows.anchor: اعلم أني قد انتخبت بصليال بن أوري بن حور من سبط يهودا وأسبغت عليه روح الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Oholiab of Dan and other wise workers received wisdom and understanding to carry out the instructions.
rows.anchor: وقد ضممت إليه آليهب بن اخسمخ من سبط دان وأحللت الحكمة والفهم في قلوب ذوي الحكمة والعقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The workers were to make the tent, ark and cover, table, lampstand, altars, basin, priestly garments, anointing oil, and sacred incense.
rows.anchor: وجميع متاع قبة المائدة وجميع متاعها والمنارة وجميع آنيتها ومذبح البخور ومذبح القرابين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After finishing his speech on Sinai, God gave Moses two stone tablets written by God's hand.
rows.anchor: دفع إلى موسى : لما فرغ من كلامه له في طور سيناء لوحي الشهادة لوحي حجارة مكتوب عليهما بيد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Moses was delayed on the mountain, the people asked for gods to lead them, not knowing what had happened to him.
rows.anchor: نتخذ لنا آلهة تسير أمامنا , لأن الرجل موسى الذي أخرجنا من أرض مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people made a calf, sacrificed to it, ate and drank, and indulged in revelry; Aaron was distressed.
rows.anchor: فذكر اتخاذهم العجل وأنهم ذبحوا له الذبائح وجلسوا يأكلون ويشربون وقاموا يلعبون ويتسافهون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Biqāʿī avoids quoting the Torah's opening wording verbatim because he sees it as too crude for Aaron's standing and as implying a deficiency that he rejects; he suspects alteration.
rows.anchor: وإنما لم أسق نص التوراة عن هذا بلفظه لأن في أول عبارته ما رأيته غضا بالنسبة إلى مقام هارون عليه السلام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Nasa'i, Abu Ya'la, Ibn Abi Hatim, and Ibn Jarir transmit Ibn Abbas's report on the fitan, which al-Biqāʿī says is not far from his interpretation.
rows.anchor: ما رواه النسائي وأبو يعلى وابن أبي حاتم وابن جرير عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما في حديث الفتون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Biqāʿī directs readers to his discussion of the relevant material in Surah Taha.
rows.anchor: فوجدته ليس بعيدا من تأويله وقد ذكرت محل الحاجة منه في سورة طه والله الموفق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God told Moses to descend because the people had corrupted their conduct, quickly left the commanded path, and made a calf to worship and sacrifice to.
rows.anchor: اهبط من ههنا لأن شعبك الذين أخرجتهم من أرض مصر أفسدوا سيرتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people identified the calf as the god who had brought Israel from Egypt.
rows.anchor: هذا إلهك يا إسرائيل الذي أخرجك من أرض مصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God called the people hard-hearted and proposed destroying them while making Moses into a great nation.
rows.anchor: قاسية قلوبهم فدعني الآن فيشتد غضبي عليهم فأقتلهم وأبيدهم وأصيرك إلى شعب عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses pleaded that God not destroy the people he had brought from Egypt, lest the Egyptians say he led them out to kill them in the mountains.
rows.anchor: ولا يقول أهل مصر : إنك إنما أخرجتهم لهلاكهم لتقتلهم بين الجبال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asked God to forgive the people's sin and remember the oath to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob to multiply their descendants and give them the land.
rows.anchor: اذكر إبراهيم وإسحاق ويعقوب عبيدك والأيمان التي أقسمت بها لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God relented and did not bring the threatened calamity on the people.
rows.anchor: فعفا الرب عن شعبه ولم ينزل بهم الشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses descended with tablets written on both faces by God's hand.
rows.anchor: واللوحان من عمل الله جل ثناؤه وخط الله مكتوب عليهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing the calf and cymbals, Moses grew angry, smashed the tablets at the mountain's foot, burned and ground the calf, and scattered its filings on water.
rows.anchor: فرمى باللوحين من يده فكسرهما في سفح الجبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Levites rallied to Moses; he ordered them to kill their brothers, companions, and kin, and they killed about three thousand men that day.
rows.anchor: فقتل من الشعب في ذلك اليوم نحو من ثلاثة آلاف رجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses told the Levites to stop, saying their zeal for God that day would bring them a blessing.
rows.anchor: كفوا أيديكم يومكم هذا من الحمية للرب لتحل عليكم البركة يومنا هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next day Moses acknowledged Israel's grave sin and said he would ask God to forgive them; he asked to be erased from God's book if they were not forgiven.
rows.anchor: فالآن إن أنت غفرت خطاياهم وإلا فامحني من سفرك الذي كتبت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God said he would erase from his book whoever sinned, and sent an angel ahead to the land of milk and honey rather than accompany the hard-necked people himself.
rows.anchor: وهذا ملاكي ينطلق أمامك إلى الأرض التي تغل السمن والعسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people mourned at the divine warning that God might destroy them on the way.
rows.anchor: فسمع الشعب هذا القول الفظيع فحزنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses pitched his tent outside the camp and called it the Tent of Meeting; anyone seeking God went there.
rows.anchor: فأخذ موسى خيمته فنصبها خارجا من العسكر وأبعدها من المحلة وسماها قبة الزمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Moses entered the tent, the cloud pillar stood at its entrance and spoke with him, while the people watched and prayed at their tent doors.
rows.anchor: كان ينزل عمود السحاب فيقف على باب القبة ويكلم موسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God spoke face-to-face with Moses as one speaks with a companion; Joshua son of Nun remained in the tent after Moses returned to camp.
rows.anchor: وكلم الرب موسى مواجهة كما يكلم المرء أخاه وصاحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses asked whom God would send with him, reminded God of his favor, and asked to know God's way.
rows.anchor: أنت يا رب أمرتني أن أصعد بهذا الشعب ولم تطلعني على من ترسل معي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promised to go before Moses, meet him, and give him rest.
rows.anchor: سر أمامي فأواعدك وأريحك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses insisted that Israel not leave unless God went with them, since God's presence distinguished them from all peoples; God agreed and promised to make Moses renowned.
rows.anchor: إلا إذا سرت بيننا فنكون أنا وشعبك منفصلين معروفين من جميع الشعوب الذين على وجه الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Moses asked to see God's glory, God promised to pass his glory before Moses and proclaim his name, showing mercy as he chose.
rows.anchor: أنا أجيز جميع مجدي وكرامتي بين يديك ويذكر اسم الرب أمامك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God said Moses could not see his face, because no human could see it and live.
rows.anchor: إنك لا تقدر على النظر إلى وجهي , لأنه لا يراني بشري فيحيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God ordered Moses to cut two replacement stone tablets and ascend Sinai alone, with no one or livestock on the mountain.
rows.anchor: نقر موسى لوحين آخرين من حجارة مثل الأولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses praised God's mercy, patience, grace, truth, and forgiveness, then prostrated and asked God to travel among Israel and forgive its sins and ill intentions.
rows.anchor: يا رب ! اللهم ربي الرؤوف الرحيم الطويل الأناة والمهل الكبير نعمته وقسطه حافظ النعمة والعدل إلى ألف حقب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God renewed the covenant before the people and promised unprecedented wonders, commanding Israel to keep his instructions and promising to drive out the Canaanites.
rows.anchor: ها أنا ذا أعهد عهدا أمام جميع الشعب وأظهر عجائب لم أظهر مثلها في الأرض كلها وفي جميع الشعوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Israel was to keep the seven-day Unleavened Bread festival in the month named الفقاج, with another version reading الفريك; the text says the Exodus occurred in that month.
rows.anchor: واحتفظ بعيد الفطير سبعة أيام كما أمرتك في أوان شهر الفقاج - وفي نسخة : الفريك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses stayed with God for forty days and nights without food or drink, while God wrote the covenant's ten commandments on stone tablets.
rows.anchor: فمكث هناك عند الرب أربعين يوما ولياليها لم يأكل طعاما ولم يشرب شرابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses returned unaware that his face shone; Aaron and Israel feared approaching him, so he called them, spoke, and covered his face with a veil afterward.
rows.anchor: فنظر هارون وجميع بني إسرائيل إلى وجه موسى ففزعوا أن يقتربوا إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God prescribed six days of work and a holy Sabbath rest on the seventh, with death for Sabbath work and no fire in homes.
rows.anchor: واليوم السابع يكون مخصوصا مقدسا , السبت يوم راحة قدس الرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God ordered contributions of gold, silver, copper, cloth, skins, and other materials for the Tent of Meeting.
rows.anchor: ثم أمرهم تعالى بالزكاة من الذهب والفضة والنحاس والقز والجلود وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God ordered the tent erected on the first day of the first month; Aaron and his sons were to be washed, vested, and anointed for an enduring priesthood.
rows.anchor: وادن بهارون وبنيه إلى باب قبة الأمد واغسلهم بالماء , والبس هارون لباس القدس وامسحه فليكهن لي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses erected the tabernacle in the second year, placed the testimony and cover, arranged the lamps, bread, altars, basin, and courtyard, and the priests washed before service.
rows.anchor: وتناول الشهادة فوضعها في التابوت , وصير الدهوق في التابوت , ووضع التطهير على التابوت من فوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cloud covered the tent and God's glory filled it, preventing Moses from entering.
rows.anchor: وتغشت السحابة قبة الزمان وامتلأت القبة مجد الرب وكرامته
